artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer k ≥ 2, define the classical van der Waerden number W(k) to be the smallest positive integer N such that every 2-coloring of {1, 2, …, N} contains a monochromatic k-term arithmetic progression. Define W*(k) to be the smallest possible cardinality |A| of a finite set A ⊂ ℤ with the property that every 2-coloring of A contains a monochromatic k-term arithmetic progression (a k-term arithmetic progression being a sequence a, a+d, a+2d, …, a+(k−1)d with d ≠ 0, all of whose terms lie in A). Note that W*(k) ≤ W(k) since A = {1, …, W(k)} is admissible, and one has W*(3) = W(3) = 9 while W*(4) ≤ 27 and W(4) = 35.

(a) Is the difference W(k) − W*(k) unbounded as k → ∞?

(b) Does W(k) − W*(k) → ∞ as k → ∞?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not surface any published resolution of the comparison between the classical van der Waerden number W(k) and the minimal-cardinality variant W*(k) (introduced by R. Graham as an open problem with a $100 prize for the first part). No source verifies that either W(k) − W*(k) is unbounded or that it tends to infinity, and no source claims a proof of boundedness either. The status appears to remain unresolved, but search evidence is inconclusive.
